source_meta._title: Strongholds will not generate in floating_islands or caves preset

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.16 Pre-release 1 in singleplayer, using a newly created custom world whose Overworld generator settings are imported from the report's JSON; commands enabled so /locate can be executed.
preconditions: A Minecraft: Java Edition installation for 1.16 Pre-release 1 is available. Use a separate game directory or otherwise avoid opening valuable worlds in this historical pre-release.
The executor can create a plain-text UTF-8 JSON file and select it through Minecraft's native file picker.

Use the floating-islands JSON from the report exactly as supplied. Do not add a structures or stronghold section, and do not substitute either attached workaround file, mcFlatStronghold.json or mcOverworldDefaults.json.
Create a new world for this reproduction; do not import the settings into or convert an existing world.
Only one /locate attempt is needed. Do not repeatedly execute the command after the first response.

steps.action: Create a plain-text UTF-8 file named MC-187357-floating-islands.json. Copy the supplied world-generation JSON into it exactly, including the seed and minecraft:floating_islands generator setting, then save the file with the .json extension rather than .txt.
steps.success_cue: MC-187357-floating-islands.json exists as a readable JSON file and contains minecraft:floating_islands without any added structures or stronghold configuration.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft: Java Edition using the installation configured for 1.16 Pre-release 1. Do not use the listed fix version, 1.16.2 Pre-release 2.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen identifies the running game as 1.16 Pre-release 1.

steps.action: From the title screen, click Singleplayer and then click Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open for a new world.

steps.action: Set Game Mode to Creative. Creative mode is not asserted by the report; it is selected only to make the command-based reproduction safe and straightforward.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen displays Game Mode: Creative.

steps.action: Click More World Options... to open the seed, structure, command, and world-import controls used by this version.
steps.success_cue: The More World Options screen is visible and includes the Import Settings control.

steps.action: Verify that Allow Cheats is ON. If the button reads Allow Cheats: OFF, click it once. Do not proceed with cheats disabled because /locate requires command permission.
steps.success_cue: The button reads Allow Cheats: ON.

steps.action: Click Import Settings to open the operating system's file-selection dialog.
steps.success_cue: A file-selection dialog is open and waiting for a JSON file to be selected.

steps.action: In the file-selection dialog, navigate to MC-187357-floating-islands.json, select it, and activate the dialog's Open or Select button.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft accepts the selected file and returns to world creation without displaying Error Importing Settings.

steps.action: If Minecraft displays a warning that imported/custom world-generation settings are experimental, accept the warning by clicking Yes or Proceed. If no warning appears, continue without changing any imported setting.
steps.success_cue: The warning is dismissed, the Create New World interface is available again, and no import error is displayed.

steps.action: Leave the imported world-generation configuration unchanged. In particular, do not add custom stronghold settings and do not replace minecraft:floating_islands with minecraft:overworld or minecraft:amplified. Click Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The world-generation loading screen appears.

steps.action: Wait for world creation and initial chunk loading to finish. Do not issue the command while the loading screen is present. Once control is available, wait until nearby terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the Overworld, floating-islands terrain is visible around the player, the loading screen is gone, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Press T, the default Open Chat control, to open the in-game chat and command-entry field.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is visible and has keyboard focus.

steps.action: Type the version-compatible stronghold location command into chat exactly as shown, including the leading slash. Do not press Enter yet.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field contains /locate stronghold exactly, with stronghold in lowercase.

steps.action: Press Enter once to submit the command, then wait until Minecraft produces a command-feedback line in chat. Do not execute the command a second time.
steps.success_cue: The /locate stronghold command has been submitted and its resulting feedback line is visible in chat.

stor.handoff_condition: The player is in the newly generated floating-islands Overworld created from the report's unmodified JSON, and /locate stronghold has just returned a feedback line in chat. Hand control to the observation subsystem to capture and evaluate that command feedback.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode. Creative mode is selected only as a practical way to enable and safely execute /locate; the generator configuration remains unchanged.

The title mentions both floating_islands and caves, but the report supplies a complete deterministic JSON configuration only for minecraft:floating_islands. This plan therefore reproduces the documented floating-islands case and does not invent a separate caves configuration.
The plan assumes the English UI labels used by Java Edition 1.16 Pre-release 1. Equivalent localized controls may have different text.
An experimental-settings confirmation may appear after importing the JSON; the precise warning presentation can depend on the affected pre-release, so that action is conditional.

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.16 Pre-release 2 in single-player, using a fresh custom world imported from the report's version-compatible world-generation JSON. Use an unmodified client, Creative mode, commands enabled, and Spectator mode for non-destructive inspection. Use an isolated game directory so the pre-release does not access unrelated worlds.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher can start the exact affected version 1.16 Pre-release 2; do not substitute 1.16 Release Candidate 1, release 1.16, or fix version 21w44a.

Download the MC-187716 attachment named worldgen_settings_export.json and keep its contents unchanged. The plan assumes this is the early attachment intended for the initial 1.16 Pre-release reproduction.

Before continuing, establish that the selected JSON defines a Nether whose generated terrain can extend above Y=127. If the file is rejected by 1.16 Pre-release 2 or does not define a taller Nether, stop rather than silently replacing or rewriting it.
Create a completely new world in 1.16 Pre-release 2. Do not reuse a world opened in 1.16 Pre-release 1, and do not upgrade the test world to another version.
Do not enable unrelated data packs, mods, or custom world-generation files.
The instructions refer to the default keyboard and mouse controls. If controls are rebound, use the bound control for the same action.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for the exact affected version 1.16 Pre-release 2 and launch it from an isolated game directory. Enable historical snapshot/pre-release versions in the launcher if the version is not initially listed.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and identifies the running game as Minecraft 1.16 Pre-release 2.

steps.action: Make the report attachment worldgen_settings_export.json available through the operating system's file chooser. Do not rename its extension, edit its JSON, or substitute either Taller Nether ZIP attachment, because those ZIP files were discussed for later snapshots.
steps.success_cue: An unchanged local copy of worldgen_settings_export.json is available for selection.

steps.action: From the title screen, select Singleplayer and then Create New World. This must be a new world rather than a re-created or converted older save.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open for a new save.

steps.action: Open More World Options and select Import Settings. In the file chooser, select worldgen_settings_export.json. Accept the experimental custom-world warning if one appears. Do not manually alter any imported generator, dimension, height, default-block, biome, or surface-builder value.
steps.exact_input: More World Options... -> Import Settings -> worldgen_settings_export.json
steps.success_cue: Minecraft accepts the JSON and returns to world creation with the imported custom world-generation settings active; no invalid-settings or data-pack error is displayed.

steps.action: Set the world to Creative mode so commands and flight-related setup are available without gathering resources. Ensure Allow Cheats is ON after importing the settings, because importing may return the interface to a different world-creation state.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Cheats: ON
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Creative mode and commands/cheats enabled.

steps.action: Optionally give the world a recognizable name, then select Create New World. Do not change the imported world-generation options before creating it.
steps.exact_input: World Name: MC-187716 1.16-pre2; Create New World
steps.success_cue: World creation begins using the imported settings.

steps.action: Wait for the player to enter the new world. Do not continue while the loading screen is visible or while nearby chunks are still appearing. Test movement briefly to confirm that the integrated server is responsive.
steps.success_cue: The player is present in the newly created world, nearby terrain is rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Enter Spectator mode so the player can inspect tall Nether terrain without mining, suffocating, falling, or modifying naturally generated surfaces. Press T to open chat, enter the command including its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds; the hotbar disappears and the player can fly through solid blocks.

steps.action: Teleport into the custom Nether at Y=160. Press T, enter the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter. Spectator mode makes the initial destination safe even if the coordinate is inside solid terrain or above an open cavern.
steps.success_cue: The view reloads in the Nether dimension and the player remains in Spectator mode near Y=160.

steps.action: Wait until the Nether terrain surrounding the destination has rendered and movement and chat respond normally. Then press F3, or Fn+F3 on keyboards where the function row is media-controlled, to open the debug overlay.
steps.success_cue: The debug overlay is visible, the current dimension is minecraft:the_nether, and the displayed player Y coordinate is approximately 160.

steps.action: Locate a biome whose affected surface-builder type is explicitly confirmed by the report. While still near Y=160, press T, enter the Soul Sand Valley locate command with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat returns coordinates for a nearby minecraft:soul_sand_valley instead of reporting that the biome could not be found.

steps.action: Read the X and Z coordinates returned by locatebiome. Press T and teleport to those X and Z coordinates while retaining Y=160. Replace only the two placeholders; keep the command's Y value at 160. This loads or generates tall Nether terrain at the vertical level relevant to the report.
steps.success_cue: The teleport completes and the player is positioned at Y=160 near the located Soul Sand Valley coordinates.

steps.action: Do not move immediately after teleporting. Wait until all nearby chunks have rendered and movement, the debug overlay, and chat update normally.
steps.success_cue: The terrain around the located coordinates is fully rendered and the integrated server is responsive.

steps.action: Use the F3 biome line to verify that the player's current position at Y greater than 127 is inside minecraft:soul_sand_valley. If the exact teleport point is on a biome boundary, move horizontally in Spectator mode near the returned coordinates while keeping Y above 127 until the biome line identifies minecraft:soul_sand_valley. If the biome cannot be reached at this height, repeat the locate command from the current Y=160 position and use the new X and Z result.
steps.success_cue: The debug overlay identifies the current biome as minecraft:soul_sand_valley while the player's Y coordinate remains greater than 127.

steps.action: Within the confirmed Soul Sand Valley, use Spectator flight to locate naturally generated solid terrain above Y=127. Use the movement controls W/A/S/D, Space to ascend, and Left Shift to descend. Look specifically for an exposed floor surface: a solid top block with air directly above it, rather than an arbitrary block inside a solid mass. Do not break or place blocks.
steps.success_cue: A naturally generated exposed floor surface in minecraft:soul_sand_valley is visible, and the F3 targeted-block coordinates place its top block at Y=128 or higher.

steps.action: Hover two to five blocks above the selected surface, center it in view, and stop all movement. Keep the F3 overlay open so the dimension, biome, player height, and targeted-block coordinates remain available. Wait until chunk rendering and movement are stable, then hand control to the observation subsystem without changing versions or modifying the terrain.
steps.success_cue: A stable, naturally generated Soul Sand Valley floor surface at Y=128 or higher is centered in view, minecraft:the_nether and minecraft:soul_sand_valley are visible in debug information, and the game is responsive.

stor.handoff_condition: The custom Nether chunk near the located Soul Sand Valley has been generated or loaded at Y=160, and the player is now stationary in Spectator mode above a naturally generated Soul Sand Valley floor surface whose top block is at Y=128 or higher. The F3 overlay remains open and the terrain has not been modified. Begin surface-composition observation now.
uncertainties: The raw contents and attachment timestamps were not supplied. The plan assumes worldgen_settings_export.json is the attachment compatible with the first listed affected version, 1.16 Pre-release 2. If Minecraft rejects it, attachment metadata or contents are required before a valid first-version reproduction can continue.
The report supplies no deterministic world seed or Nether coordinates. The locatebiome command and limited high-altitude Spectator search are therefore necessary practical inferences.

The report confirms minecraft:nether_forest, minecraft:soul_sand_valley, and minecraft:basalt_deltas surface-builder types. This plan selects minecraft:soul_sand_valley as one confirmed test case and does not use the only tentatively identified minecraft:nether type.

The report does not provide a formal numbered Steps to Reproduce section. The minimum path of importing a taller-Nether configuration, generating Nether chunks above Y=127, and positioning the player at a confirmed affected biome surface was reconstructed from the description, comments, and attachment names.

Web verification confirmed that the affected release family exposed experimental custom-world import during world creation and that a fresh 1.16 Pre-release 2 world should be used rather than a world opened in 1.16 Pre-release 1. Command-based navigation and biome selection remain practical implementation choices rather than report-mandated actions.

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.16 Release Candidate 1 in singleplayer, using the report's attached custom-world JSON. Use Creative mode with commands enabled so the supplied /setblock command can be executed safely. No dedicated server or additional player is required.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher must have an installation for the exact affected version "1.16 Release Candidate 1" available.

Download the report attachment intended for the original 1.16 Release Candidate 1 reproduction to an accessible local directory. Based on the attachment names and report chronology, use "mcDefaultTest.json" rather than the later "mcDefaultTest-1.json" or "mcDefaultTest-2.json" revisions.
Preserve the attachment exactly as supplied; do not rewrite, modernize, or otherwise alter its dimension-type or noise-generator JSON.
Use a new disposable singleplayer world; no seed or coordinates are specified by the report.
Commands must be enabled. Selecting Creative mode is a practical way to enable commands and avoid survival hazards during the dimension transition.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation whose version is exactly "1.16 Release Candidate 1", then launch it.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft: Java Edition main menu has loaded under the selected 1.16 Release Candidate 1 installation.

steps.action: Confirm that the unmodified report attachment "mcDefaultTest.json" is present in a local directory that can be reached from the operating system's file-selection dialog.
steps.success_cue: The JSON file is locally available and has not been edited.

steps.action: From the main menu, select "Singleplayer".
steps.success_cue: The Select World screen is open.

steps.action: Select "Create New World".
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open.

steps.action: Cycle the "Game Mode" button until it displays "Creative". Creative mode is not stated as a bug requirement; it is selected to provide command access and prevent survival hazards from interfering with the test.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen displays "Game Mode: Creative".

steps.action: Verify that "Allow Cheats" is set to "ON". If Creative mode enabled it automatically, leave it enabled; otherwise click the button until it reads "ON".
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows that cheats or commands are enabled.

steps.action: Select "More World Options..." to expose the world-generation controls used by this historical version.
steps.success_cue: The More World Options screen is visible, including an "Import Settings" control.

steps.action: Select "Import Settings".
steps.success_cue: The operating system's JSON file-selection dialog opens.

steps.action: In the file-selection dialog, navigate to and select the unmodified attachment named "mcDefaultTest.json", then confirm the selection with the dialog's Open/Select action.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft begins reading the selected custom world-generation settings.

steps.action: If Minecraft displays an experimental-world warning, or a recoverable parsing/validation warning that explicitly offers an option to continue, choose the option that continues with the imported settings. Do not edit the JSON in response to the warning. If the message provides no way to continue and returns to the menu, stop rather than substituting a different world configuration.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft returns to the world-creation flow with the imported custom settings accepted and still allows the world to be created.

steps.action: Select "Create New World" to generate a new world from the imported JSON settings.
steps.success_cue: The world-generation/loading screen appears.

steps.action: Wait until the Overworld finishes loading. Do not continue while the terrain is blank or player input is unresponsive.
steps.success_cue: Overworld terrain is rendered around the player and normal movement and camera controls respond.

steps.action: Remain in a stable, fully loaded location and stop moving. The supplied command uses relative coordinates, so the block space containing the player's current position is the target location.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary, the surrounding terrain is loaded, and there is no other loading screen active.

steps.action: Press the default chat key T to open in-game chat. If controls have been rebound, use the control assigned to Open Chat.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Do not change the namespace, coordinates, or block identifier. Because the end portal is placed in the block space at the player's current position, remain there and allow portal contact to initiate the dimension transition.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and an End-dimension loading transition begins; if the portal block is briefly visible before loading, the player is intersecting it.

steps.action: Wait for the End-dimension transition to finish. Do not begin evaluation while terrain is still loading.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the End environment, with the arrival area and surrounding End terrain rendered, and movement and camera controls are responsive.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just completed the portal transition into the End generated by the imported custom-world JSON, the End terrain has rendered, and player controls are responsive. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately without performing additional commands, exploration, or entity spawning.
uncertainties: The supplied report lists three attachments but does not include their file contents, upload timestamps, or explicit version-to-file mapping. The plan selects "mcDefaultTest.json" for the first affected version because it is the original unsuffixed attachment referenced by the initial reproduction; verify attachment metadata if it is available to the execution system.

A later comment states that the original file eventually became invalid because it lacked the required coordinate_scale property. That comment concerns later tested versions; the plan does not add coordinate_scale or otherwise modify the file when reproducing in the first affected version.

The exact wording and buttons of the experimental or parsing warning are not included in the report. Continue only when Minecraft itself presents a recoverable continuation option; do not bypass a fatal error by changing the test JSON.
The report does not prescribe a game mode. Creative mode is selected only as a practical execution choice that enables the supplied command and minimizes unrelated hazards.
No seed, spawn coordinates, graphics settings, server configuration, or additional datapacks are specified for the recommended 1.16 Release Candidate 1 reproduction.

source_meta._title: Adding a biome to a datapack shifts biome IDs in existing chunks

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 20w30a in a single-player world using the integrated server. Use one persistent world for both datapack states. Creative mode is selected as a practical implementation choice so a Nether portal can be constructed without unrelated resource gathering. Do not open the test world in the fix version 21w38a or any other Minecraft version during this procedure.
preconditions: A Minecraft: Java Edition installation profile for exactly snapshot 20w30a is available.
The two original Mojira attachments are available as separate ZIP files with the exact filenames "Incendium_v3.0.3.zip" and "Incendium v3.1.zip".
The ZIP files have not been renamed, merged, or replaced by another Incendium release.
The executor can copy and remove files from the test world's datapacks directory.
Use a new disposable test world. Do not perform the reproduction in a valuable existing save.
Keep Minecraft version 20w30a selected before every load of the test world.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an isolated Java Edition installation that launches exactly snapshot 20w30a. Start the game with this installation and verify that the title screen identifies the running version as 20w30a.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft: Java Edition is at the main menu and displays version 20w30a.

steps.action: From the main menu, choose Singleplayer, then Create New World. Give the world a recognizable name such as "MC-202036-Repro" and set Game Mode to Creative. Leave the seed unspecified because the report provides no required seed.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen shows Creative mode and the chosen test-world name.

steps.action: Open the Data Packs screen from the world-creation screen, then choose Open Pack Folder. Copy the exact attachment "Incendium_v3.0.3.zip" into the folder that opens. Do not copy "Incendium v3.1.zip" yet, and do not extract the ZIP.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation datapack folder contains "Incendium_v3.0.3.zip" and does not contain "Incendium v3.1.zip".

steps.action: Return to the Minecraft Data Packs screen. Move Incendium v3.0.3 from the Available list to the Selected list by clicking its arrow or datapack icon. If a validation or experimental-world warning appears, confirm it without changing the Minecraft version.
steps.success_cue: Incendium v3.0.3 appears in the Selected datapacks list and Minecraft permits returning to the world-creation screen.

steps.action: Create the world. Wait until the player appears and surrounding terrain has rendered. Do not proceed while the world is still showing a loading screen or while player movement is unresponsive.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the new Creative-mode Overworld, terrain is visible, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory with the inventory control, which is E by default. Use the Search Items tab to place Obsidian and Flint and Steel into hotbar slots, then close the inventory with E or Esc. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the game screen.
steps.success_cue: Obsidian and Flint and Steel are visible in the player's hotbar.

steps.action: Select the Obsidian hotbar slot. Build a vertical rectangular Nether portal frame with a 2-block-wide by 3-block-high empty interior; a complete frame is 4 blocks wide and 5 blocks high when its four corners are included. Ensure the interior contains only air.
steps.success_cue: A complete upright obsidian frame with a clear 2-by-3 interior stands near the player.

steps.action: Select Flint and Steel in the hotbar, aim at an interior bottom block of the obsidian frame, and use the item with right-click. Wait for the purple portal field to fill the frame.
steps.success_cue: The portal interior is filled with the animated purple Nether portal field.

steps.action: Walk into the purple portal field with the movement controls, using W by default, and remain inside it until dimension transfer begins.
steps.success_cue: The dimension-loading screen appears and the player is transferred away from the Overworld.

steps.action: Wait until the Nether terrain surrounding the destination has fully rendered and the player can move normally. Do not leave the Nether or replace the datapack at this stage.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the Nether, nearby terrain is visible, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Press F3 to open the debug screen and inspect the displayed biome resource identifier. If the current position is not in a custom biome supplied by the datapack, move or fly through newly generated Nether terrain until the biome line shows a non-vanilla biome identifier rather than an identifier beginning with "minecraft:". In Creative mode, double-tap Space to begin flying and use W to move. Do not assume a specific custom-biome identifier because the report does not provide one.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing or flying in a generated Nether chunk whose F3 biome line displays a custom, non-"minecraft:" biome identifier.

steps.action: While remaining near the identified custom-biome area, press F3+G to display chunk borders. Move across several adjacent chunk borders so multiple Nether chunks are generated and loaded under Incendium v3.0.3. A practical minimum is to cross a border in each cardinal direction from the selected target chunk and then return to that target chunk. Wait after each movement until nearby terrain has rendered.
steps.success_cue: The target custom-biome chunk and several adjacent Nether chunks have rendered under Incendium v3.0.3, and the player has returned to the target chunk.

steps.action: With the player back in the target custom-biome chunk, press F3 if necessary and record the exact X, Y, and Z coordinates and the displayed custom-biome identifier. Press F2 to save a screenshot of the debug screen as a location record. Leave the player at this position.
steps.success_cue: The target coordinates and original custom-biome identifier have been recorded, a screenshot has been saved, and the player remains in the target Nether chunk.

steps.action: Press Esc and choose Save and Quit to Title while the player is still in the recorded target Nether chunk. Wait until the main menu is displayed so the world is no longer running.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The main menu is visible and the test world is closed with the player's saved position inside the generated Nether target chunk.

steps.action: Before changing datapacks, create a backup copy of the entire test-world folder in a separate location. The backup is only for recovery; continue the reproduction using the original world folder, not the backup.
steps.success_cue: A separate backup copy exists and the original test-world folder remains the active save.

steps.action: From Singleplayer, select the same test world, choose Edit, and use Open World Folder. Open its "datapacks" subfolder. Remove "Incendium_v3.0.3.zip" from that folder and copy in the exact second attachment, "Incendium v3.1.zip". Do not leave both versions installed simultaneously.
steps.success_cue: The original world's datapacks folder contains "Incendium v3.1.zip" and no longer contains "Incendium_v3.0.3.zip".

steps.action: Return to Minecraft and verify once more that the running launcher installation is still exactly 20w30a. In Singleplayer, select the original "MC-202036-Repro" world; do not create a new world and do not open the backup.
steps.success_cue: The original test world is selected for loading in Minecraft 20w30a after the datapack replacement.

steps.action: Open the selected original world with Incendium v3.1 installed. Confirm any datapack or experimental-world prompt required to continue, but do not use a safe-mode option that disables the datapack. Wait until loading finishes, the player appears at the previously recorded Nether coordinates, the previously generated surrounding chunks are rendered, and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The same save is running in 20w30a with Incendium v3.1 installed, and the player is at the recorded location inside the previously generated Nether custom-biome area.

stor.handoff_condition: The original world has just finished loading in Minecraft 20w30a with only "Incendium v3.1.zip" installed, and the player is positioned at the recorded coordinates inside Nether chunks that were generated under "Incendium_v3.0.3.zip". The old surrounding chunks are rendered and movement is responsive; hand control to the observation subsystem now.
uncertainties: The report does not supply a world seed, target coordinates, or a specific custom-biome identifier. The procedure therefore locates any Incendium custom biome under v3.0.3 and records its coordinates before replacing the datapack.
The report does not specify a game mode. Creative mode is used only as a practical way to build a Nether portal and traverse terrain without unrelated resource gathering.

The report says to load "some chunks" but does not state an exact number or shape. The plan loads the target custom-biome chunk and several adjacent chunks to satisfy that condition without generating an excessive area.
The attachment contents are not included in the supplied report text. This plan assumes the executor has the two original Mojira ZIP attachments and that they are valid for the report's reproduction.

The report does not specify whether the player must leave the target area and return after replacing the datapack. Saving the player inside the target Nether chunk makes those existing chunks load immediately when the same world is reopened.

Minecraft 20w30a menu labels or datapack warning text may differ slightly by launcher platform or language; the required file order remains v3.0.3 for initial Nether generation followed by v3.1 in the same world.

source_meta._title: Strongholds do not generate in certain customized worlds despite /locate saying otherwise

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 20w51a, single-player integrated server, a newly created Creative-mode world with commands available, and the final working revision of the report attachment named 210612.json imported as the world's custom generation settings.
preconditions: Install and launch an unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 20w51a profile. Use a separate game directory if necessary so that newer installations do not overwrite this historical profile's files or options.

Download the final available revision of 210612.json from the MC-210612 attachments. The comments state that an earlier supplied revision produced parser errors and was later replaced, so do not use a locally retained earlier revision with the same filename.
Keep 210612.json as a standalone JSON file in a location accessible through the operating system's file-selection dialog; do not place it in the saves directory as though it were a complete world.
Use a new single-player world. Do not substitute a normally generated world, manually recreate the JSON settings, or change the imported world-generation configuration.
Commands must be available. Selecting Creative mode during world creation should provide command access in this single-player test.

If importing 210612.json produces parser or validation errors in 20w51a, stop rather than creating a world with fallback/default settings; such a world would not preserve the report's required customized generation.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation whose version is exactly Java Edition snapshot 20w51a, then start that installation.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and the displayed version is 20w51a.

steps.action: From the main menu, open the single-player world list.
steps.success_cue: The Select World screen is visible.

steps.action: Select Create New World to open the world-creation screen.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is visible and is configuring a new world rather than an existing save.

steps.action: Change Game Mode until it is set to Creative. If an Allow Cheats control is independently available, ensure it is set to ON.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Cheats: ON if shown
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen identifies the selected game mode as Creative and commands will be available in the world.

steps.action: Open the additional world-generation controls by selecting More World Options.
steps.success_cue: The screen shows world-generation controls, including the control used to import world settings.

steps.action: Select the Import Settings control. This is the historical custom-world-settings import function available during world creation in this version family.
steps.success_cue: The operating system's file-selection dialog opens.

steps.action: In the file-selection dialog, navigate to and select the final downloaded report attachment, then confirm the file selection.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft begins processing 210612.json and either presents an experimental-settings confirmation or returns to world creation with the imported settings.

steps.action: If Minecraft displays a warning that custom or experimental world settings may be unstable, use the confirmation control to continue with the imported settings.
steps.success_cue: The warning closes and Minecraft returns to the new-world configuration flow without abandoning the imported settings.

steps.action: Confirm that the import completed without a parser, validation, or settings-loading error. Do not manually change the imported seed, biome distribution, dimension settings, structure settings, default block, or effects after import.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World flow remains usable after the import and no message states that 210612.json failed to load.

steps.action: Select Create New World to generate the customized world from the imported settings.
steps.success_cue: World generation begins using the imported configuration.

steps.action: Wait for the world to finish loading. Do not begin the command sequence while the loading screen is still present.
steps.success_cue: The player is controllable in the new world, nearby terrain has rendered, and the Creative-mode hotbar and crosshair are visible.

steps.action: Press the chat/command key, which is T by default, to open the in-game command input.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open at the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Enter the report's locate command exactly, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports the position of the nearest stronghold rather than reporting a syntax, permission, or unknown-structure error.

steps.action: Read the locate result and record the reported X and Z coordinates exactly. If the result displays a coordinate triplet such as [X, ~, Z], X is the first value and Z is the third value; the tilde means that no fixed Y coordinate was supplied.
steps.success_cue: The executor has stored the locate result's exact X and Z values for use in the teleport command.

steps.action: Press T again to open a fresh command input.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready for the teleport command.

steps.action: Teleport horizontally to the reported locate position. Replace <LOCATED_X> and <LOCATED_Z> with the exact first and third coordinate values from the locate result; retain the tilde for Y so the player's current vertical coordinate is preserved. Include the leading slash, then press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player's horizontal position changes to the reported X and Z coordinates and the command does not produce a syntax or permission error.

steps.action: Wait at the destination until the surrounding customized terrain has rendered and player movement and commands respond normally.
steps.success_cue: Chunks around the located X/Z position are rendered and the game accepts movement without active destination-loading pauses.

steps.action: Press T to open the command input for the game-mode change.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open.

steps.action: Switch the player to Spectator mode by entering the command with its leading slash and pressing Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds, the normal Creative hotbar is no longer present, and the player can fly through solid blocks.

steps.action: Without moving significantly away from the located X/Z coordinates, aim the camera downward. Use the coordinates display if it was already enabled, or the F3 debug screen if needed, to keep X and Z close to the recorded locate values.
steps.exact_input: F3 if coordinate guidance is needed
steps.success_cue: The camera is aimed into the ground while the player remains in Spectator mode at or very near the reported stronghold X/Z position.

steps.action: Begin flying straight downward through the terrain at the located position using the descend control, Left Shift by default. Continue only until the observation subsystem takes control; do not return to the surface, generate another world, or run /locate again.
steps.success_cue: The Spectator-mode player has entered the underground terrain beneath the X/Z position returned by /locate and can visually inspect generated blocks while descending.

stor.handoff_condition: The player is in Spectator mode at the X/Z position returned by /locate stronghold, the destination chunks are fully loaded, and the player has just begun descending through the underground terrain. Hand control to the observation subsystem to inspect structure generation around the locate target.
uncertainties: The raw report does not include the contents of 210612.json, so its seed, exact dimension configuration, biome list, structure configuration, and default block cannot be reproduced manually from the supplied text.

The comments state that an earlier attachment revision caused parser errors and that a new working world-generation import was later supplied, but the raw export lists only one attachment filename and does not identify attachment revisions. The plan therefore requires the final available revision associated with the issue.

Although 20w51a is the first listed affected version and is therefore the recommended version, the report does not explicitly establish that the final replacement revision of 210612.json remains syntactically compatible with 20w51a. If it is rejected, do not silently move to another affected version or allow default generation; the attachment-to-version mapping must first be resolved.
The report supplies neither a fixed seed nor fixed stronghold coordinates in text. The reproduction therefore obtains the target coordinates dynamically from /locate stronghold in the imported world.

The teleport command was not supplied verbatim by the reporter. Using /tp @s <LOCATED_X> ~ <LOCATED_Z> is a practical implementation of the report's instruction to teleport to the coordinates while avoiding an invented fixed Y coordinate.
